title: Eval signal troubleshoot and guardrail runbook with Auric Systems
summary: Weekly POC sync to investigate an uptick in false-negative safety flags and a small drop in label-level accuracy. SE walked through latest scoring heatmap, team agreed to run a targeted 10k prompt benchmark, tune guardrail thresholds, and rehearse rollback playbook next Tuesday. Action owners assigned.
action_items: Diego Ramos: run 10k prompt benchmark on dedicated-quant model and share raw CSV (due 2026-06-09)
Maya Chen: send updated pricing and pilot extension options, include Dedicated burst note (due 2026-06-05)
Evan Park: provide subset of 500 high-risk prompts for safety tuning (due 2026-06-07)
Jade Kim: confirm SOC2 scope questions and share encryption/KMS contact (due 2026-06-08)
Priya Nambiar: schedule rollback rehearsal and invite infra (due 2026-06-09)
next_steps: SE to push a guardrail threshold tweak to staging and monitor false-positive rate for 48h
Customer to run canary with 5% traffic after threshold tweak
Joint rollback drill next Tue 10:00am PT
Share runbook and benchmark results in shared drive link: https://redwood.example/s/auric-poc-runbook
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03 09:15 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM) -- Evan (Auric Head ML), Lina (SRE), Ben (PM), Jade (Security)

[00:00] Maya: ok hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick check in, we'll start with what you observed this week Evan?
[00:22] Evan: yeah thanks Maya, so we saw a bump in false-negative safety flags — basically examples that previously passed now get blocked, and our label-level accuracy dipped like 3 points on the customer-intent set, not huge but enough to break some flows.
[00:45] Diego: hmm can you give an example, is it related to longer prompts or the new quantized variant you switched to last week?
[01:03] Evan: it's mostly mid-length chat prompts, 40-80 tokens. We did flip from fp16 to the quantized-8b variant to save cost. Also we added a prefix caching layer, maybe KV cache warmed differently.
[01:28] Lina: we also noticed latency jitter when batching spikes, but that's separate.
[01:34] Diego: got it, thanks. I pulled the heatmap this morning, can I share screen?
[01:40] Ben: go for it
[01:45] Diego: ok so this is the confusion matrix for the scoring function — see the blue cluster here where safety triggers overlap with intent classifications, looks like tightening threshold pushed some marginal positives into the blocked bucket. Might be a calibration drift after the quant roll.
[02:12] Evan: that matches our logs. Any chance the kernel selection or sequence-length padding changed in infra?
[02:20] Diego: infra did a minor change — the runtime switched a kernel variant to better throughput, maybe different attention tiling, but that shouldn't change logits normally. Could interact with quantization.
[02:38] Jade: from security side we need to keep rollback options — if we adjust thresholds we can't leave customers in a state where data gets exposed. Walk me through how you plan to roll back.
[02:50] Priya: we'll use canary routing and automatic fallback to the previous model variant. We have a rollback playbook, Diego can show the steps.
[03:05] Diego: yes, step 1 snapshot config, step 2 change thresholds in staging, step 3 observe metrics for 48 hours, step 4 canary 5% traffic, step 5 either rollforward or fallback to pinned model.
[03:20] Ben: can the pinned model be pinned per-route? We need to pin sensitive routes only.
[03:26] Maya: yes you can pin model versions per route in Redwood Dedicated and in our hosted you can set per-route policies.
[03:33] Evan: ok, so we need to run a benchmark focused on our prompt set, especially those 500 high-risk prompts we flagged.
[03:42] Diego: agreed — I'm proposing a 10k mixed prompt run that includes the high risk 500, a 2k synthetic stress set, and the rest sampled from production. That should surface calibration drift and latency SLO hits.
[04:00] Lina: what's the expected runtime for that? We need to schedule GPU time.
[04:06] Diego: on Dedicated with batch size tuned, about 2-3 hours wall clock, Hosted might take longer due to queuing.
[04:12] Evan: we can allocate Dedicated test window.
[04:18] Maya: I'll add pricing notes about Dedicated burst to the follow-up.
[04:22] Jade: on the SOC2/KMS front: we want to confirm the key management flow when you do caching — are tokens persisted encrypted?
[04:32] Diego: yes, KV cache persists optionally, it's encrypted at rest with customer KMS in Private deployments. On Hosted we use envelope encryption; we can map to your HSM keys for Dedicated via the KMS bridge.
[04:48] Jade: send that doc please.
[04:51] Maya: will do.
[04:53] Evan: another question — scoring thresholds, can they be per-customer or per-route? We want per-customer adjustments for high-risk accounts.
[05:02] Diego: yes, thresholds are policy-level; you can scope them per-tenant or per-route. It requires a small config layer change, we can push a patch to separate policies for the 10 high-risk accounts.
[05:15] Ben: any regressions in generation quality after quantization?
[05:20] Diego: we measured a small BLEU-ish drop on the paraphrase task, but for intent classification it's more calibration than fluency.
[05:30] Evan: ok that tracks.
[05:32] Maya: let's capture concrete next steps — Diego you run the 10k benchmark, Evan you'll share the 500 prompts, Maya sends pricing and extension, Jade shares KMS contact, Priya will schedule rollback drill.
[05:45] Evan: quick follow up, what about false positives — the guardrail is too aggressive in some cases and we saw many manual overrides. Can thresholds be softened without exposing sensitive outputs?
[06:00] Diego: yes that's the tuning tradeoff — we can increase threshold to reduce false positives, but then we need compensating checks: post-filtering, redact rules, or a secondary verifier model. We recommend a two-tier approach: loosen threshold + rerank with a conservator model for flagged outputs.
[06:24] Ben: what's the cost implication of adding a secondary verifier?
[06:28] Diego: modest increase in per-request tokens, but we can run verifier only for borderline cases — profiling suggests maybe 12–18% cost uplift on the flagged subset, not across all traffic.
[06:42] Jade: fine as long as audit logs and encryption are preserved.
[06:47] Maya: ok real quick can we set success criteria for the benchmark? Evan?
[06:52] Evan: yes — target: reduce false-negative rate back to baseline within 48h after tuning, keep false-positives under 5% of flagged volume, latency p95 < 450ms for interactive routes.
[07:08] Diego: I'll instrument the dashboards and share a heatmap and threshold proposal by Friday.
[07:15] Priya: I'll send a calendar invite for the rollback rehearsal Tue 10am PT, incl infra and product.
[07:21] Jade: and I'll provide the KMS contact and SOC2 scoping note.
[07:26] Maya: perfect. Anything else?
[07:30] Ben: just please include how to revert the prefix cache if warm-state causes differences.
[07:35] Diego: noted — step included: invalidate prefix cache and repopulate from snapshot as part of rollback.
[07:42] Maya: thanks all, recap and we'll close.
[07:46] Evan: thanks everyone
[07:48] End meeting.
